title: Text is lost when a run of backticks is closed by a longer run
spec:
This is the Python-Markdown library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q`. When a run of backticks is followed later by a longer run of backticks, the text in between is thrown away and an empty code element is produced. Input: `markdown.markdown('a ``` b ````` c')` Expected: `

a ``` b ````` c

` Actual: `

a c

` A code span only closes with a run of exactly the same number of backticks, so neither run here forms a code span and all the text should be kept literally. Similarly `a `` b ``` c` currently gives `

a b c

` but should stay as plain text. The case where the closing run is shorter must keep working as it does now: `a ``` b `` c` renders as `

a ` b c

`.
acceptance: The reported input renders as expected with no text lost
A longer closing run never closes a code span; the shorter-closing-run case is unchanged
